problems: The main open result is a race: whether '2D coordinate diagram. Checking optional 3D view…' is announced on EC-014 first load. The executor saw three outcomes: not surfaced (S1, S5, S3F), spoken (S3, S3X), or surfaced but read after the text changed, so the next message was spoken twice (S2). My seven runs saw two of them: spoken in S1, S1r2, S5 and S3F; never surfaced in S3, S3r2 and S2. The DOM gap between the two states does not predict which happens: spoken at 90, 162, 528 and 644 ms, not surfaced at 120, 416 and 452 ms. A claim that EC-014 announces exactly one first-load message, or always the 'Checking…' message, is not supported.

Orca page-load messages vary between runs. 'Loading.  Please wait.' appears in some runs and not others. The 'Page has N landmarks, M headings…' numbers depend on how much of the page had rendered: I got 8/12/66, 8/18/76, 8/39/117, 9/35/110, 9/63/1/149, 9/67/1/157 and 9/68/1/159.

Say All chunk counts and absolute 'played' times cannot be compared with the executor's. The default speech-dispatcher setup cannot open audio here (no PulseAudio, no /dev/snd), and utterances then never complete, which would stall Say All. I used my own speechd config (scripts/sdconf) routing ALSA's file plugin into rt_sink.py, which consumes 22050 Hz mono 16-bit audio in real time. The executor's pacer is different and about 10% faster (an 11.0 s utterance against 12.3 s in mine), and its step lengths also differ.

Chromium does not trust the agent-proxy CA, so the 26 raw.githubusercontent.com source files were fetched with curl (TLS verified) and served to the page through CDP Fetch.fulfillRequest. The page checked their sha256 itself and showed 'Source projections and displayed source bytes verified'. three.js was served or blocked the same way, and its SRI hash matched THREE_CDN.integrity.

The S3 Orca debug log contains 3 lines with binary junk, and some debug text there was overwritten. No speech record was lost: every speech-dispatcher queue entry matched an Orca SPEECH OUTPUT or Say All record (extract.py lists any unmatched speechd message as SPEECHD-ONLY, and none appeared).
Not replicated: the XTest variants S3X and S4X.

The first runner script (run_all.sh) printed a syntax error after its last scenario because I edited it while it was running; S1, S3 and S4 had all completed. Later batches used run_all2.sh. Chrome's background requests to Google hosts were refused by the proxy, which did not affect the runs.
compare.py compares items as sets, so it misses a count difference when other differences are present. I checked the S2 'spoken once against twice' difference by hand.
